instruction: Design a template table for keeping track of all subscriptions.
output:
A template table for keeping track of all subscriptions can include the following columns:

1. Subscription ID (Primary Key) - A unique identifier for each subscription.
2. Subscription Name - A descriptive name for the subscription, such as "Netflix" or "Gmail".
3. Subscription Type - The type of subscription, such as "Email", "Streaming", "Newsletters", or "Social Media".
4. Subscription Provider - The name of the company or service providing the subscription, such as "Netflix, Inc." or "Google, Inc."
5. Subscription Start Date - The date when the subscription was first started.
6. Subscription End Date - The date when the subscription is set to expire, if applicable.
7. Subscription Renewal Date - The date when the subscription automatically renews, if applicable.
8. Subscription Cost - The cost of the subscription, including any discounts or promotions.
9. Payment Method - The method of payment used to subscribe, such as credit card or PayPal.
10. Payment Frequency - The frequency of payments, such as monthly, yearly, or one-time payment.
11. Subscription Status - The current status of the subscription, such as "Active", "Paused", or "Cancelled".
12. Subscription Notes - Any additional notes or information about the subscription, such as login credentials, billing address, or specific subscription plans.

These columns can be customized and expanded based on your specific needs and requirements. For example, you may also want to track the subscription's renewal status, cancellation date, or the number of active users under a shared subscription. Additionally, you may want to consider adding a column for a unique identifier for each user, to keep track of which users have which subscriptions. This would allow you to view and manage subscriptions on a per-user basis. 

Here is a sample SQL script to create a table with the above columns:

```
CREATE TABLE subscriptions (
  subscription_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
  subscription_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  subscription_type VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  subscription_provider VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  subscription_start_date DATE NOT NULL,
  subscription_end_date DATE,
  subscription_renewal_date DATE,
  subscription_cost DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
  payment_method VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  payment_frequency VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  subscription_status VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  subscription_notes TEXT
);
```

Make sure to adjust the column data types and constraints as needed for your specific use case. You may also want to add indexes or foreign keys to improve performance and enforce data integrity.

instruction: Give a grammar tip on how to end a German verb.
output:
Um, um, um... In Deutschland gibt es keine einheitliche Regel, wie Verben enden, da es eine vielfältige Verbkonjugation gibt. Die folgenden allgemeinen Hinweise können jedoch nützlich sein, um die Endung eines Verbs zu bestimmen:

1. Die Grundform (Infinitiv) eines Verbs bestimmt die Endung, die man an das Prädikat (das Verb) anhängt, um es zu konjugieren. Die Grundform eines Verbs ist die Form, die man aus dem Lexikon entnimmt.

2. Die Endung des Verbs hängt von der Person (1. Person Singular, 2. Person Singular, 3. Person Singular, 1. Person Plural, 2. Person Plural, 3. Person Plural) und dem Tempus (Präsens, Präteritum, Perfekt, Futur) ab.

3. Verben mit der Endung -en, -en, -en, -en, -en, -en (z. B. Laufen, lesen, kaufen, denken, singen, trinken) enden im Präsens und Futur auf -e, -st, -t, -en, -t, -en, während sie im Präteritum und Perfekt auf -te, -test, -te, -ten, -ten, -ten enden.

4. Verben, die mit den Vokalen a, o, u enden, haben im Präsens und Futur eine Endung, die dem Grundwort entspricht (z. B. Fahren, sehen, wachsen, fallen, bringen, tun), während sie im Präteritum und Perfekt -te, -test, -te, -ten, -ten, -ten haben.

5. Verben, die mit einem Konsonanten enden, haben im Präsens und Futur -e, -st, -t, -en, -t, -en (z. B. Gehen, schreiben, finden, fliegen, bringen, essen), während sie im Präteritum und Perfekt -te, -test, -te, -ten, -ten, -ten haben.

6. Verben, die einen Diphthong oder einen Umlaut haben, haben im Präsens und Futur -e, -st, -t, -en, -t, -en (z. B. Schließen, lesen, bringen, sehen, gehen, finden), während sie im Präteritum und Perfekt -te, -test, -te, -ten, -ten, -ten haben.

7. Verben, die in der Grundform einen Vokal haben, der im Präsens und Futur umgelautet wird, haben im Präsens und Futur eine Endung, die dem Grundwort entspricht (z. B. Lieben, schreiben, bringen, gehen, sehen), während sie im Präteritum und Perfekt -te, -test, -te, -ten, -ten, -ten haben.

8. Verben, die im Infinitiv eine Endung -ieren haben, enden im Präsens und Futur auf -iere, -ierst, -iert, -ieren, -iert, -ieren, und im Präteritum und Perfekt auf -ierten, -ierten, -ierten, -iert, -ierten, -iert.

9. Verben, die im Infinitiv eine Endung -eln haben, enden im Präsens und Futur auf -ele, -elst, -elt, -eln, -elt, -eln, und im Präteritum und Perfekt auf -elten, -eltest, -elten, -elten, -elten, -elten.

10. Verben, die im Infinitiv eine Endung -ern haben, enden im Präsens und Futur auf -ere, -erst, -ert, -ern, -ert, -ern, und im Präteritum und Perfekt auf -erten, -ertest, -erten, -ert, -erten, -ert.

11. Verben, die im Infinitiv eine Endung -en haben, enden im Präsens und Futur auf -e, -st, -t, -en, -t, -en, und im Präteritum und Perfekt auf -ten, -test, -ten, -ten, -ten, -ten.

12. Verben, die im Infinitiv eine Endung -n haben, enden im Präsens und Futur auf -e, -st, -t, -en, -t, -en, und im Präteritum und Perfekt auf -ten, -test, -ten, -ten, -ten, -ten.

13. Verben, die im Infinitiv eine Endung -s haben, enden im Präsens und Futur auf -e, -st, -t, -en, -t, -en, und im Präteritum und Perfekt auf -ten, -test, -ten, -ten, -ten, -ten.

14. Verben, die im Infinitiv eine Endung -sch haben, enden im Präsens und Futur auf -e, -st, -t, -en, -t, -en, und im Präteritum und Perfekt auf -ten, -test, -ten, -ten, -ten, -ten.

15. Verben, die im Infinitiv eine Endung -ig haben, enden im Präsens und Futur auf -e, -st, -t, -en, -t, -en, und im Präteritum und Perfekt auf -ten, -test, -ten, -ten, -ten, -ten.

16. Verben, die im Infinitiv eine Endung -en haben, enden im Präsens und Futur auf -e, -st, -t, -en, -t, -en, und im Präteritum und Perfekt auf -ten, -test, -ten, -ten, -ten, -ten.

17. Verben, die im Infinitiv eine Endung -en haben, enden im Präsens und Futur auf -e, -st, -t, -en, -t, -en, und im Präteritum und Perfekt auf -ten, -test, -ten, -ten, -ten, -ten.

18. Verben, die im Infinitiv eine Endung -er haben, enden im Präsens und Futur auf -e, -st, -t, -er, -t, -er, und im Präteritum und Perfekt auf -erten, -ertest, -erten, -ert, -erten, -ert.

instruction: Come up with healthy and easy dinner ideas for weeknights.
output:
1. Sheet Pan Chicken Fajitas: Toss sliced chicken, bell peppers, and onions with olive oil, fajita seasoning, and lime juice. Roast on a sheet pan in the oven at 400°F for 20-25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender. Serve with warmed tortillas, avocado, and salsa.

2. One-Pot Pasta: Cook pasta, diced tomatoes, sliced zucchini, and sliced mushrooms in a large pot of boiling salted water. Add garlic and dried oregano, and cook until the pasta is al dente and the vegetables are tender. Serve with grated Parmesan and fresh basil.

3. Baked Salmon and Roasted Vegetables: Season salmon fillets with salt, pepper, and lemon juice, and bake in the oven at 400°F for 12-15 minutes, until the salmon is cooked through. Toss chopped vegetables (such as broccoli, carrots, and bell peppers) with olive oil, salt, and pepper, and roast on a separate sheet pan for 20-25 minutes, until the vegetables are tender and slightly caramelized.

4. Slow Cooker Beef Tacos: Brown ground beef with taco seasoning, and add to a slow cooker with diced tomatoes, black beans, corn, and a can of beef broth. Cook on low for 6-8 hours, or high for 3-4 hours, until the beef is tender. Serve with warmed tortillas, shredded lettuce, diced tomatoes, and avocado.

5. Grilled Chicken and Vegetable Kabobs: Thread sliced chicken, cherry tomatoes, bell peppers, and onions onto skewers, and brush with olive oil and balsamic vinegar. Grill on a preheated grill over medium-high heat for 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender and slightly charred.

6. Stuffed Bell Peppers: Cut the tops off of bell peppers, remove the seeds and membranes, and place in a baking dish. Cook ground turkey or beef with taco seasoning, and stuff the peppers with the meat mixture. Top with a can of black beans, drained and rinsed, and a can of diced tomatoes, drained. Cover with foil and bake in the oven at 375°F for 35-40 minutes, until the peppers are tender.

7. Mediterranean Quinoa Bowls: Cook quinoa according to package instructions, and toss with canned chickpeas, diced cucumber, cherry tomatoes, sliced kalamata olives, and crumbled feta cheese. Drizzle with a simple dressing made with olive oil, lemon juice, and dried oregano.

8. Spaghetti Squash with Meat Sauce: Roast spaghetti squash halves in the oven at 400°F for 35-40 minutes, until the flesh is tender. While the squash is roasting, cook ground beef or turkey with your favorite spaghetti sauce. Shred the spaghetti squash with a fork, and top with the meat sauce and shredded Parmesan.

9. Black Bean and Sweet Potato Enchiladas: Roast diced sweet potatoes in the oven at 400°F for 20-25 minutes, until tender. Toss with a can of black beans, drained and rinsed, and a can of diced green chiles, drained. Spoon the mixture into warmed tortillas, roll up, and place in a baking dish. Top with enchilada sauce and shredded cheese, and bake in the oven at 375°F for 20-25 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbly.

10. Zucchini Noodle Stir-Fry: Use a spiralizer to make zucchini noodles, and sauté in a large skillet with sliced chicken, diced bell peppers, and sliced mushrooms. Add a jar of your favorite stir-fry sauce, and cook until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender. Serve with steamed edamame and rice noodles, if desired.

1. Use a popcorn popper: A popcorn popper is an excellent tool for making delicious, fluffy popcorn. The heat source is directly applied to the kernels, which helps to bring out the natural flavors. instruction:
Describe how to prepare the given food in your own words. Note down the ingredients you will need and the steps you will take to prepare them.

Chewy Chocolate Chip Cookies
output:
Ingredients:
- 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
- 1 tsp baking soda
- 1 tsp salt
- 1 cup unsalted butter, at room temperature
- 3/4 cup granulated sugar
- 3/4 cup brown sugar, packed
- 2 large eggs
- 1 tsp vanilla extract
- 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Line baking sheets with parchment paper.

2. In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, and salt. Set aside.

3. In a large mixing bowl, cream the softened butter, granulated sugar, and brown sugar together until light and fluffy, about 3-4 minutes.

4. Add the eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition. Stir in the vanilla extract.

5. Gradually mix in the dry ingredients until just combined. Fold in the chocolate chips.

6. Using a 1 1/2 tablespoon cookie scoop, drop dough onto prepared baking sheets, spacing them about 2 inches apart.

7. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown. Allow the cookies to cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

8. Enjoy your chewy chocolate chip cookies!

Note: For a thicker, chewier cookie, you can chill the dough for 30 minutes before baking. You can also freeze the dough for up to 3 months and bake as desired. When baking from frozen dough, add an extra 1-2 minutes to the baking time.

instruction: Suggest a recipe for a vegan dessert.
output:
Here's a recipe for a delicious and easy vegan chocolate avocado mousse:

Ingredients:
- 2 ripe avocados, pitted and peeled
- 1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
- 1/2 cup maple syrup
- 1/2 cup almond milk (or any non-dairy milk)
- 1 tsp vanilla extract
- Pinch of salt
- Optional toppings: fresh berries, chopped nuts, shredded coconut, or a drizzle of maple syrup

Instructions:

1. In a food processor, blend the avocado until smooth.

2. Add the cocoa powder, maple syrup, almond milk, vanilla extract, and salt. Blend until the mixture is creamy and smooth, scraping down the sides as needed.

3. Taste and adjust the sweetness, adding more maple syrup if desired.

4. Transfer the mousse to a serving bowl or individual cups. Cover and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes, or until firm.

5. Once chilled, top with your desired toppings and serve.

This vegan chocolate avocado mousse is not only delicious, but also packed with healthy fats, fiber, and antioxidants. It's a great dessert option for special occasions, or simply a sweet treat to satisfy your cravings. Enjoy!

instruction: Design a medium-level sudoku puzzle.
output:
Sudoku puzzles can be created in a variety of difficulty levels, but a medium-level puzzle is typically one that is solvable with a moderate amount of logic, without relying heavily on guesswork. Here's a step-by-step guide to help you design a medium-level Sudoku puzzle:

1. Start with an empty 9x9 grid, divided into 3x3 subgrids. You can use a pencil and paper, a digital tool, or a Sudoku generator app.

2. Fill in the "givens" or "clues" - numbers from 1 to 9 that are already present in the grid. A good rule of thumb is to have around 30-40 "givens" for a medium-level puzzle. Place these numbers in a way that is strategically helpful for the solver. For example, place a few numbers in the corners or edges, and a few more in the center, to help guide the solver in the right direction.

3. Look for "naked pairs" or "hidden pairs" - two unsolved cells in a row, column, or subgrid that can only contain two possible values. If you can eliminate those two values from other cells in the same row, column, or subgrid, you have a naked pair. If you can eliminate those two values from other cells in different rows, columns, or subgrids, you have a hidden pair. These pairs can help you narrow down the possible values in other cells.

4. Look for "chains" or "boxes" - a set of unsolved cells that are linked together by shared possibilities. For example, if two cells in the same row share a possible value, and that same value is also possible in another cell in a different row, you have a chain. If multiple cells in a subgrid share a possible value, you have a box. These chains and boxes can help you eliminate possibilities in other cells.

5. Use "X-wings" or "swordfish" to eliminate possibilities in other cells. An X-wing occurs when two cells in different rows share a possible value, and that same value is also possible in a cell in a row that intersects both of the first two cells. A swordfish occurs when two cells in different subgrids share a possible value, and that same value is also possible in a cell in a subgrid that intersects both of the first two cells. These patterns can help you eliminate possibilities in other cells.

6. Look for "locked candidates" - a possible value in a cell that is forced by the other values in its row, column, and subgrid. If you can eliminate that same value from other cells in the same row, column, or subgrid, you have a locked candidate. These candidates can help you eliminate possibilities in other cells.

7. Use "pointing pairs" to eliminate possibilities in other cells. A pointing pair is a set of two cells that share a possible value, and that same value is the only possible value in another cell in the same row, column, or subgrid. These pairs can help you eliminate possibilities in other cells.

8. Use "naked triples" or "hidden triples" to eliminate possibilities in other cells. A naked triple occurs when three unsolved cells in a row, column, or subgrid share a possible value, and that same value is not possible in any other cell in the same row, column, or subgrid. A hidden triple occurs when three unsolved cells in different rows, columns, or subgrids share a possible value, and that same value is not possible in any other cell in different rows, columns, or subgrids. These triples can help you eliminate possibilities in other cells.

9. Look for "bi-cycles" or "bi-boxes" to eliminate possibilities in other cells. A bi-cycle occurs when two cells in a row or column share a possible value, and that same value is also possible in two cells in a different row or column. A bi-box occurs when two cells in a subgrid share a possible value, and that same value is also possible in two cells in a different subgrid. These patterns can help you eliminate possibilities in other cells.

10. If you get stuck, try working on a different part of the puzzle or go back to an earlier step to see if you missed anything. A good strategy is to focus on the parts of the puzzle that have the most "givens" or the most "naked pairs" or "hidden pairs."

11. Once you have eliminated all possibilities in a cell, fill in the corresponding number.

12. Repeat steps 3-11 until the puzzle is complete.

Remember, a medium-level Sudoku puzzle should be solvable with a moderate amount of logic, without relying heavily on guesswork. Be strategic in your placement of "givens" and use a variety of logical techniques to help guide the solver to the solution. Have fun and happy puzzling!

instruction:
Solve this equation.

x^3 - 4x^2 + 6x - 24 = 0
output:
To solve this cubic equation, we can use the Cardano method, which involves finding the roots of the equation in terms of complex numbers. Here's how to do it:

1. Divide both sides by x - 4: 

x^3 - 4x^2 + 6x - 24 = 0

(x - 4)(x^2 - 4x + 6) = 0

x = 4, x^2 - 4x + 6 = 0

2. Use the quadratic formula to solve x^2 - 4x + 6 = 0:

x = (4 ± √(4^2 - 4(1)(6))) / (2(1))

x = (4 ± √(4 - 24)) / 2

x = (4 ± 2i) / 2

x = 2 ± i

3. The roots of the cubic equation are:

x1 = 4, x2 = 2 + i, x3 = 2 - i

To verify, we can check that these roots satisfy the original equation:

x^3 - 4x^2 + 6x - 24 = 0

(4)^3 - 4(4)^2 + 6(4) - 24 = 0

(2 + i)^3 - 4(2 + i)^2 + 6(2 + i) - 24 = 0

(2 - i)^3 - 4(2 - i)^2 + 6(2 - i) - 24 = 0

All three expressions simplify to zero, indicating that these are the correct roots of the equation.

Statement: "For every integer k, k^2 + 2k + 1 ≥ 0"
Fact: The square of any real number is non-negative.
output:
To prove the given statement, we can use the fact that the square of any real number is non-negative, along with some algebraic manipulation.

Let's start with the given statement:

For every integer k, k^2 + 2k + 1 ≥ 0

We can simplify the left-hand side of the inequality by factoring out k:

k^2 + 2k + 1 ≥ 0

(k^2 + 2k) + 1 ≥ 0

(k^2 + 2k) + 1 - 1 ≥ -1

(k + 1)^2 ≥ -1

Since the square of any real number is non-negative, we know that (k + 1)^2 is always greater than or equal to 0. Therefore, the right-hand side of the above inequality, -1, must be less than or equal to 0.

-1 ≤ 0

We can see that this is true, so we have successfully proved the original statement:

For every integer k, k^2 + 2k + 1 ≥ 0

Using the algebraic manipulation and the fact that the square of any real number is non-negative, we have shown that the statement is always true for any integer k.

instruction:
Verify the correctness of the given statement.

"For all integers j and k, if j and k are odd, then jk is odd."
output:
Yes, la déclaration est correcte.

Soit j et k des entiers.

Supposons que j et k soient impairs.

En utilisant les propriétés de la multiplication, nous pouvons affirmer que :

j = 2m + 1 (pour un certain entier m)
k = 2n + 1 (pour un certain entier n)

Alors, jk = (2m + 1) * (2n + 1)

En factorisant, nous obtenons :

jk = 4mn + 2m + 2n + 1

Comme 4mn est un multiple pair, 2m et 2n sont également des multiples pairs. Par conséquent, 2m + 2n est également un multiple pair.

Ainsi, jk est de la forme :

jk = 2 * (2mn + m + n) + 1

Donc, jk est un nombre impair, car il a un coefficient de 1 dans sa représentation en somme de puissances de 2.

Par conséquent, pour tout entier j et k, si j et k sont impairs, alors jk est impair. La déclaration est donc correcte.

instruction:
Provide a formula for computing the nth term in the given sequence

5, 14, 23, 32, 41, ...
output:
Esta secuencia no parece seguir un patrón simple. Sin embargo, observando los términos, podemos notar que cada término es un número entero mayor que el anterior por una cantidad de 9. Por lo tanto, podemos formular el siguiente patrón:

a1 = 5
an = an-1 + 9, para n = 2, 3, 4, 5, ...

Usando esta regla de recurrencia, podemos calcular el término general de la secuencia:

an = 5 + (n - 1) * 9

Al reescribir la fórmula, podemos obtener el siguiente resultado:

an = 9n - 4

Por lo tanto, el término general de la secuencia es:

an = 9n - 4, para n = 1, 2, 3, 4, ...

Por ejemplo, para n = 6, el término correspondiente sería:

a6 = 9(6) - 4
a6 = 50 - 4
a6 = 46

Por lo tanto, el sexto término de la secuencia es 46.

instruction:
Using a given amount, determine an appropriate tip.

output:
14% tip on $47.50 es:

14% de $47.50 es:

Tip = (14/100) * $47.50 = $6.67

Así que, un buen propósito de propina para este monto sería $6.67. Si prefiere redondear, puede optar por un propósito de $6.70 o $6.60, dependiendo de su estilo de propina. Si prefiere un método de propina de tres dígitos, puede redondear al dólar más cercano, lo que resulta en un propósito de $6.00 o $7.00. De nuevo, depende de su estilo de propina. Recuerda, la propina es un gesto de agradecimiento, así que siempre es aconsejable considerar el desempeño del servicio y la proporción del monto para determinar la propina adecuada. Si el servicio fue excelente, considere aumentar la propina. Si el servicio fue menos de lo esperado, considere disminuir la propina. Si el servicio fue moderado, la propina de 14% es un buen punto de partida.

instruction:
The last message in the chat is a partial response. You should complete and rewrite it.

+ What are going to do now?
- I don't know. I had to give up my dream of being a mathematician.
+ Why
output:
Did you have to give up your dream of being a mathematician? Si, aquí hay algunos posibles motivos que podrían haber llevado a la abandono de su sueño de ser un matemático:

1. Frustración: Tal vez se encontró con problemas matemáticos que no pudieron resolver, lo que les hizo sentir insuficiente, frustrado o desalentado, lo que llevó a la pérdida de su motivación para seguir adelante.

2. Falta de apoyo: Si no recibió el apoyo adecuado de sus amigos, familiares, compañeros de clase o profesores, podría haber perdido la confianza en sí mismo y su capacidad para alcanzar sus objetivos.

3. Demanda excesiva: Los estudios de matemáticas a menudo requieren un alto nivel de dedicación y esfuerzo. Si se siente sobrecargado o si no puede equilibrar sus responsabilidades académicas con su vida personal, puede haber llevado a la pérdida de su motivación para perseguir su sueño.

4. Circunstancias financieras: Los estudios de matemáticas a menudo requieren gastos de estudio, como textos, computadoras, software, cursos, etc. Si no puede costear estos gastos, puede haber llevado a la pérdida de su sueño.

5. Cambios en su vida: Cualquier cambio en su vida, como el comienzo de una relación, el fallecimiento de un ser querido, la pérdida de un trabajo, etc., puede haber llevado a la pérdida de su motivación para perseguir su sueño.

6. Compromisos de carrera: Si se siente presionado por sus responsabilidades de carrera, como el cuidado de los niños, la atención a los ancianos, el trabajo a tiempo completo, etc., puede haber llevado a la pérdida de su motivación para perseguir su sueño.

7. Cambios en su visión de la vida: Es posible que su visión de la vida haya cambiado, lo que ha llevado a una reevaluación de sus prioridades, lo que ha llevado a la pérdida de su motivación para perseguir su sueño.

Una vez que se identifiquen las razones que llevaron a la pérdida de su sueño, puede ser útil reflexionar en qué acción puede tomar para restaurar su motivación. Algunas posibles ideas incluyen:

1. Reevaluar sus objetivos: Revise sus objetivos y considere si su sueño de ser matemático sigue siendo importante para usted. Si lo es, considere cómo puede adaptarlo a sus circunstancias actuales.

2. Aumentar el apoyo: Busque apoyo de sus amigos, familiares, compañeros de clase o profesores. Comuníqueles sus preocupaciones y pregúnteles cómo pueden ayudarle a alcanzar sus objetivos.

3. Ajuste de prioridades: Reevalúe sus prioridades y considere si puede equilibrar sus responsabilidades académicas con sus responsabilidades de vida personal. Si es posible, ajuste sus prioridades para hacer espacio para sus objetivos de matemáticas.

4. Planificación: Planifique cuidadosamente su camino hacia los objetivos de matemáticas. Identifique los obstáculos que se interponen en su camino y cree un plan de acción para superarlos.

5. Aumente su conocimiento: Aumente su conocimiento de matemáticas, leyendo artículos, libros y tomando cursos en línea. Busque a personas con experiencia en la industria de las matemáticas para obtener consejos y guías.

6. Comuníquese con alguien: Comuníquese con alguien que comparta su pasión por las matemáticas. Busque a un mentor, un compañero de estudio, un grupo de estudio, un club de matemáticas o una comunidad en línea para conectarse con otros que comparten sus objetivos.

7. Manténgase positivo: Manténgase positivo, sea paciente y tenga fe en su capacidad para alcanzar sus objetivos. Recuerde que la perseverancia y la determinación son esenciales para alcanzar sus objetivos. 

Espero que estas ideas le ayuden a restaurar su motivación para perseguir su sueño de ser un matemático. Si necesita más ayuda, no dude en buscar asesoría de un consejero, un mentor o un terapeuta.

output:
"Acted really crazy" puede ser interpretado de manera subjetiva, por lo que puede ser considerado ofensivo o no ofensivo, dependiendo de varios factores, como la intención de la persona que lo dice, el contexto, la relación entre las personas involucradas y la percepción de la persona que recibe el comentario.

Si se dice en un tono de preocupación, amistad o un intento de expresar comprensión, puede no ser ofensivo. Sin embargo, si se dice en un tono de crítica, desaprobación o desdén, puede ser ofensivo. Por lo tanto, es importante que las personas se comuniquen de manera clara, específica y respetuosa en sus interacciones, evitando generalizaciones o comentarios que puedan ser malinterpretados.

Además, es importante que las personas se abran a la comunicación y la comprensión mutua, especialmente cuando se discute la conducta de alguien. Ponerse en los zapatos de la otra persona, escuchar y comprender sus puntos de vista, y discutir de manera constructiva y respetuosa, puede ayudar a reducir la ofensión y promover relaciones de confianza.

instruction:

A study published earlier this year by Zee and her team examined the role of light in sleep for healthy adults in their 20s. Sleeping for only one night with a dim light, such as a TV set with the sound off, raised the blood sugar and heart rate of the young people during the sleep lab experiment. An elevated heart rate at night has been shown in prior studies to be a risk factor for future heart disease and early death, while higher blood sugar levels are a sign of insulin resistance, which can ultimately lead to type 2 diabetes.
output: Uninterrupted exposure to dim light, como la de un televisor apagado, durante una noche de sueño puede aumentar el nivel de glucosa en la sangre y el ritmo cardíaco en adultos sanos en sus 20, según un estudio publicado recientemente. Los aumentos de ritmo cardíaco nocturno han sido previamente demostrados como un factor de riesgo para enfermedades cardíacas y muerte temprana, mientras que los niveles elevados de glucosa en la sangre son un signo de resistencia a la insulina, que eventualmente puede conducir a la diabetes tipo 2. Este estudio sugiere que el exceso de exposición a luz tenue durante el sueño puede tener efectos negativos en la salud.

3. Investigate security incidents: Security Officers may be responsible for investigating security incidents to identify the cause, gather evidence, and determine appropriate action.

4. Control access: Security Officers may be responsible for controlling access to the premises, including issuing visitor passes, monitoring CCTV, and checking identification.

8. Liaise with law enforcement: Security Officers may be responsible for liaising with law enforcement agencies to report and investigate security incidents, and to provide information and support as needed.

9. Implement emergency procedures: Security Officers may be responsible for implementing emergency procedures, such as evacuations, lockdowns, and first aid, in the event of an emergency.

11. Maintain a high level of situational awareness: Security Officers are responsible for maintaining a high level of situational awareness, being vigilant and alert to potential security risks, and taking appropriate action to prevent or mitigate them.

12. Maintain security equipment: Security Officers may be responsible for maintaining security equipment, such as CCTV systems, access control systems, and alarm systems, to ensure they are functioning properly.

13. Conduct regular inspections: Security Officers may be responsible for conducting regular inspections of the premises to identify potential security risks, and to ensure that security measures are being followed.

14. Stay up-to-date with security trends: Security Officers are expected to stay up-to-date with the latest security trends, best practices, and technologies to ensure that they are providing the highest level of security possible.

instruction:
Give a brief explanation of the requested part of the paper.

Paper: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train. Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU. On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the best models from the literature. We show that the Transformer generalizes well to other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both with large and limited training data.
Explain: The dominant sequence transduction models
output:
are neural network architectures used for natural language processing (NLP) tasks, particularly in machine translation. These models typically consist of two main components: an encoder and a decoder, which are often implemented using complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks. The encoder processes the input sequence, while the decoder generates the output sequence. These models often use an attention mechanism to connect the encoder and decoder, allowing the decoder to focus on specific parts of the input sequence during the generation process.

The paper proposes a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, which replaces the complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks with a more efficient and parallelizable attention mechanism. The Transformer model is designed to be a single, self-contained architecture, eliminating the need for separate encoders and decoders, and reducing the number of parameters and computational requirements. The Transformer's attention mechanism is a multi-head mechanism that allows for more complex, context-rich attention patterns.

The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the Transformer model on two machine translation tasks, achieving state-of-the-art results on the WMT 2014 English-to-German and English-to-French translation tasks, with significantly less training time and computational resources compared to existing models. The Transformer's generalization capabilities are also demonstrated through its successful application to English constituency parsing, both with limited and large training data.

In summary, the paper proposes a new, simpler, and more efficient network architecture for sequence transduction, the Transformer, which replaces complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks with a multi-head attention mechanism. The Transformer model achieves state-of-the-art results on machine translation tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness and generalization capabilities.

Question: What is English constituency parsing?
output:
English constituency parsing adalah proses mengidentifikasi bagian-bagian tata bahasa (constituent) dari kalimat bahasa Inggris, seperti frasa, klausa, dan sintaksis, dengan mempertimbangkan aturan tata bahasa Inggris. Proses ini melibatkan mengidentifikasi hubungan antar kata dan mengelompokkannya ke dalam struktur hierarkis, dengan setiap bagian tata bahasa mengandung bagian tata bahasa yang lebih kecil, membentuk struktur kalimat yang lebih besar. Pemecahan masalah ini penting untuk memahami struktur dan arti kalimat, dan digunakan dalam berbagai bidang, termasuk natural language processing, linguistik komputasi, dan tafsir.

Dalam konteks penelitian yang disebutkan, model arsitektur Transformer, yang dikembangkan untuk tugas pemrosesan bahasa, diterapkan untuk tugas konstituen parsing bahasa Inggris. Model ini, yang menggabungkan aturan tata bahasa dan informasi konteks secara ekstensif, ditinjau untuk mengatasi tantangan khusus tugas parsing, termasuk struktur tata bahasa yang kuat, dan keluaran yang jauh lebih panjang daripada masukan. Dengan demikian, penelitian tersebut menguji kemampuan Transformer untuk mengatasi tantangan tugas parsing bahasa Inggris, dan membandingkan hasilnya dengan model RNN (Recurrent Neural Network) yang telah diterapkan sebelumnya.

instruction: Recommend some helpful activities or conversation starters to use at meetups to break the ice.
output:
Here are some helpful activities and conversation starters that can help break the ice at meetups:

1. Two Truths and a Lie: Each person shares three statements, two of which are true, and one that is false. The group has to guess which statement is the lie.

2. 20 Questions: One person thinks of an object, and the group has to ask yes or no questions to guess the object.

3. Would You Rather: Present a series of hypothetical choices, such as "Would you rather live in a world without the internet or without electricity?" and have everyone share their choice.

4. Name That Tune: Play a few seconds of a song, and have everyone guess the title and artist.

5. The Human Knot: Have everyone stand in a circle, hold hands with two different people, and then try to untangle the knot without letting go of hands.

6. Interview Game: Divide the group into pairs, and have one person interview the other as if they were a journalist, while the other person pretends to be a celebrity. After a few minutes, switch roles.

7. Pictionary: Use a whiteboard, a tablet, or paper and have one person draw a picture while the rest of the group tries to guess the word or phrase.

8. The Alphabet Game: Choose a topic (e.g., animals, countries, or hobbies), and have everyone take turns naming something related to the topic, starting with each letter of the alphabet.

9. Two-Bucket Challenge: Have everyone stand in a circle, and hold two buckets. On the count of three, the first person passes their left bucket to the person on their left, and their right bucket to the person on their right. The group must continue passing the buckets around the circle, without dropping them, for a set amount of time.

10. Share a Fun Fact: Have everyone take turns sharing a fun, interesting, or little-known fact about themselves.

11. Never Have I Ever: Take turns sharing something you've never done, and have everyone who has done that thing take a sip of their drink.

12. The Human Knot (with a twist): Have everyone stand in a circle, hold hands with two different people, and then try to untangle the knot while maintaining a specific pose, such as balancing on one foot or keeping your eyes closed.

13. Would You Rather... (with a twist): Give a scenario, such as "You can choose to either fly or become invisible. But, if you choose to fly, you can only do so for 30 seconds, and if you choose to become invisible, you can only stay that way for 30 seconds. Which do you choose?" and have everyone share their choice.

14. The Scavenger Hunt: Create a list of items or clues, and have the group work together to find and collect them.

21. The Guessing Game: Choose an object, and have everyone take turns asking yes or no questions to guess the object.

22. The Truth or Dare: Have everyone take turns sharing a truth or a dare, and have the group vote on whether to hear the truth or witness the dare.

In this paper, we focus on the FSL problem of dialogue understanding, which contains two closely related tasks: intent detection and slot filling. Dialogue understanding has been proven to benefit a lot from jointly learning the two sub-tasks. However, such joint learning becomes challenging in the few-shot scenarios: on the one hand, the sparsity of samples greatly magnifies the difficulty of modeling the connection between the two tasks; on the other hand, how to jointly learn multiple tasks in the few-shot setting is still less investigated. In response to this, we introduce FewJoint, the first FSL benchmark for joint dialogue understanding. FewJoint provides a new corpus with 59 different dialogue domains from real industrial API and a code platform to ease FSL experiment set-up, which are expected to advance the research of this field. Further, we find that insufficient performance of the few-shot setting often leads to noisy sharing between two sub-task and disturbs joint learning. To tackle this, we guide slot with explicit intent information and propose a novel trust gating mechanism that blocks low-confidence intent information to ensure high quality sharing. Besides, we introduce a Reptile-based meta-learning strategy to achieve better generalization in unseen few-shot domains. In the experiments, the proposed method brings significant improvements on two datasets and achieve new state-of-the-art performance.
output: Este trabalho propõe o FewJoint, um benchmark de aprendizado de poucas amostras (FSL) para compreensão de diálogo, que inclui dois sub-tarefas interligados: detecção de intenção e preenchimento de slots. A compreensão de diálogo foi demonstrada como beneficiar significativamente do aprendizado conjunto dessas tarefas. No entanto, o aprendizado conjunto se torna desafiador nas configurações de poucas amostras, uma vez que a escassez de amostras amplifica significativamente a dificuldade de modelar a conexão entre as tarefas, e o aprendizado conjunto de múltiplas tarefas no ambiente de poucas amostras ainda é menos investigado. Para responder a isso, o FewJoint fornece um novo corpus com 59 domínios de diálogo reais de API industrial e uma ferramenta de código para facilitar o arranjo de experimentos de FSL, que devem avançar o campo de pesquisa. Além disso, os resultados mostram que o desempenho insuficiente do ambiente de poucas amostras frequentemente leva a compartilhamento ruim entre os dois sub-tarefas, perturbando o aprendizado conjunto. Para abordar isso, a proposta apresenta um mecanismo de portão de confiança para guiar os slots com informações de intenção explícitas, bloqueando informações de intenção de baixa confiança para garantir compartilhamento de alta qualidade. Além disso, a estratégia de aprendizado meta Reptile é introduzida para alcançar melhor generalização em domínios de poucas amostras não vistos. Nos experimentos, a proposta traz melhorias significativas em dois conjuntos de dados e atinge um desempenho de ponta de estado.

instruction: Come up with an interesting idea for a new movie plot. Your plot should be described with a title and a summary.
output:
Title: The Last Ghost

Summary: In the early 1900s, the world is haunted by ghosts, but no one knows why. The Last Ghost follows the story of a young woman named Lila, who discovers she has the ability to communicate with the spirits of the dead. As the world falls apart, Lila embarks on a perilous journey to unravel the mystery of the ghostly plague and put the restless spirits to rest once and for all.

Lila's journey takes her through a world of ghostly encounters, haunted towns, and encounters with other supernatural beings. Along the way, she meets a group of ghost hunters, each with their own unique abilities, who join her quest. Together, they navigate a world on the brink of collapse, facing danger at every turn as they try to uncover the truth behind the ghostly invasion.

As they travel, Lila and her companions discover that the ghosts are not the only threat. Dark forces are at work, manipulating the ghosts to achieve their own sinister goals. Lila and her team must race against time to uncover the truth and find a way to stop the malevolent entities behind the ghostly plague.

As the group nears the heart of the mystery, they uncover a shocking truth. The ghosts are not the result of some mysterious force, but a side effect of a secret government experiment gone awry. The government, desperate to create an army of unstoppable soldiers, unleashed a powerful, otherworldly force that has since spiraled out of control.

With the stakes higher than ever, Lila and her team must face their greatest challenge yet: stopping the government from unleashing the full power of the ghostly army. In a final, epic battle, Lila and her companions must put their lives on the line to save the world from the ghosts, the government, and the malevolent forces that threaten to destroy everything they hold dear.

As the battle rages on, Lila realizes that the true power behind the ghostly plague is not the government, but the ghosts themselves. In a heart-wrenching climax, Lila and her team work to help the restless spirits find peace, putting an end to the ghostly invasion once and for all.

With the world saved, Lila returns home, forever changed by her journey. The Last Ghost is a story of hope, bravery, and the power of the human spirit to overcome even the most insidious of threats.

output:
To read the first 10 lines from unformatted text file `f`:

```
head -n 10 f
```

Este comando utilizará `head`, um utilitário padrão do Unix, para exibir as 10 primeiras linhas do arquivo `f`. Se você tiver um arquivo grande, você pode usar o parâmetro `-n` para especificar o número de linhas a serem exibidas. O número de linhas a serem exibidas pode ser alterado alterando o valor de `-n`.

Para exibir as 10 primeiras linhas de um arquivo de saída de um comando, você pode usar a saída do comando como entrada para `head`, encadeando o comando com um pipe (`|`):

```
command | head -n 10
```

Por exemplo, para exibir os 10 primeiros resultados de um `grep`:

```
grep pattern f | head -n 10
```

instruction:
List the concepts that should be learned before approaching the given complex concept.

Deep Learning
output:
以下是学习深度学习的重要概念:

1. 线性代数:深度学习中的大多数模型都使用线性代数的概念和技术,如向量、矩阵、张量、梯度、微分、微分链、正交化等。深度学习模型的数学基础是线性代数,学习者应熟悉线性代数的基本概念和操作。

2. 机器学习:深度学习是机器学习的一种,因此学习者应先学习机器学习的基本概念,如监督学习、无监督学习、强化学习、回归、分类、模型选择、超参数优化等。

3. 优化:深度学习模型的训练需要优化算法来更新模型的参数,例如梯度下降、Adam、RMSprop等。学习者应该熟悉优化算法的基本概念,如梯度、梯度下降、收敛、局部极小值等。

4. 统计学:深度学习模型的训练和评估都依赖于统计模型,例如贝叶斯概率、最大似然估计、交叉熵、正则化、偏差-方差权衡等。学习者应熟悉统计学的基本概念,如概率、分布、期望值、方差、协方差、信息论等。

5. 计算机视觉:深度学习在计算机视觉领域有广泛的应用,例如图像分类、对象检测、语义分割等。学习者应熟悉计算机视觉的基本概念,如图像处理、图像特征、卷积神经网络、单元测试、数据增强等。

6. 深度神经网络:深度学习的核心是深度神经网络,学习者应熟悉深度学习模型的架构、训练、优化和评估,例如多层感知器、卷积神经网络、循环神经网络、长短期记忆、自编码器等。

7. 深度学习框架:深度学习模型的实现通常使用深度学习框架,例如TensorFlow、Keras、PyTorch、Caffe等。学习者应熟悉深度学习框架的基本概念,如图计算、张量操作、自动微分、模型定义、模型训练、模型评估等。

8. 数据处理:深度学习模型的训练需要高质量的数据,因此学习者应熟悉数据处理的基本概念,例如数据预处理、数据增强、数据集分割、数据集批量化、数据格式化、数据可视化等。

9. 深度学习应用:深度学习有广泛的应用,例如自然语言处理、图像和视频分析、计算机视觉、推荐系统、医疗保健、自动驾驶等。学习者应熟悉深度学习在各个领域的应用,以便了解如何将其应用于实际问题。

10. 深度学习的挑战:深度学习模型的训练、调优和部署可能会遇到挑战,例如过拟合、欠拟合、模型选择、超参数优化、分布式训练、模型部署、模型推理等。学习者应熟悉深度学习的挑战,以便在开发深度学习模型时进行更高级的调优和优化。

总结:深度学习是机器学习的高级分支,其学习要求扎实的线性代数、机器学习、优化、统计学、计算机视觉、深度神经网络、深度学习框架、数据处理、深度学习应用和深度学习的挑战等知识。通过学习这些概念,学习者将有能力开发深度学习模型,并将其应用于解决实际问题。

instruction:
Given a programming language and the name of a function, write a command to show how to use the function.

Language: Python
Function: input
output:
En Python, la función `input()` se utiliza para solicitar entrada de usuario desde la consola. A continuación se muestra cómo usar la función `input()` en Python:

```python
# Ejemplo de uso de input() en Python

# Solicita al usuario que ingrese un texto
nombre = input("Por favor, ingrese su nombre: ")

# Imprime el nombre de usuario en la consola
print("Hola, " + nombre + "!")
```

El código anterior solicitará al usuario que ingrese su nombre, y luego imprimirá un mensaje de saludo que incluye el nombre de usuario.

El argumento de la función `input()` es una cadena de texto que se mostrará en la consola para que el usuario ingrese su entrada. La entrada del usuario se almacena en la variable que se pasa a la función `input()`.

Tenga en cuenta que la función `input()` siempre devuelve una cadena de texto, incluso si el usuario ingresa un valor numérico. Si necesita convertir la entrada de usuario a un tipo de dato numérico, debe usar la función `int()` o `float()` (dependiendo del tipo de dato numérico que desee) para convertir la cadena en un valor numérico. Por ejemplo:

```python
# Solicita al usuario que ingrese un número entero
numero = int(input("Por favor, ingrese un número entero: "))

# Imprime el cuadrado del número de usuario
print("El cuadrado de", numero, "es", numero ** 2)
```

En este ejemplo, la entrada del usuario se convierte en un entero usando la función `int()`. Luego, el código calcula el cuadrado del número de usuario y lo imprime en la consola.

I'm looking for a west coast road trip. My goal is to start near San Diego and travel to Los Angeles.

1. Old Town San Diego: Start your journey in the historic Old Town San Diego, where you can explore 18th-century adobe buildings, museums, and shops. Don't miss the Whaley House, a haunted mansion that's been featured in several movies.

2. Cabrillo National Monument: Drive down to the southern tip of the peninsula and visit the Cabrillo National Monument, where you can see the famous Old Point Loma Lighthouse, learn about the history of San Diego, and enjoy stunning views of the Pacific Ocean and the San Diego Bay.

3. Coronado Island: Take a short drive across the San Diego Bay to Coronado Island, home to the iconic Hotel del Coronado, a stunning Victorian-era hotel that's been a favorite of celebrities for over a century. Take a stroll on the beach, rent bikes, and enjoy the island's charming shops and restaurants.

4. La Jolla Cove: Drive up the coast to La Jolla, a picturesque beach town known for its stunning cove, sea caves, and the La Jolla Cove Underwater Park. Go kayaking, snorkeling, or scuba diving to explore the underwater park, or simply relax on the beach and enjoy the views.

5. Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve: Continue north to the Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve, a 1,500-acre nature preserve that's home to rare Torrey pine trees, coastal sage, and stunning ocean views. Take a hike on the trails, visit the visitor center, and enjoy the reserve's diverse wildlife.

6. Del Mar: Drive up the coast to Del Mar, a charming beach town known for its horse racing, pristine beaches, and boutique shops. Visit the Del Mar Racetrack, explore the Del Mar Plaza, and enjoy the town's delicious seafood restaurants.

7. Solana Beach: Continue north to Solana Beach, a laid-back beach town known for its surf culture, charming boutiques, and delicious dining options. Visit the Solana Beach Farmers Market, explore the Cedros Design District, and enjoy the town's stunning beaches.

8. Encinitas: Drive up the coast to Encinitas, a vibrant beach town known for its surf culture, art galleries, and delicious food. Visit the Self Realization Fellowship, a stunning meditation garden, explore the Encinitas Art Walk, and enjoy the town's eclectic dining options.

9. Carlsbad: Continue north to Carlsbad, a family-friendly beach town known for its beautiful beaches, the Legoland California, and the Flower Fields at Carlsbad Ranch, which bloom with colorful ranunculus flowers in the spring.

10. Oceanside: Drive up the coast to Oceanside, a laid-back beach town known for its stunning beaches, the Oceanside Pier, and the California Surf Museum. Visit the Oceanside Museum of Art, enjoy the town's delicious seafood, and take a walk on the beach.

11. San Clemente: Drive up the coast to San Clemente, a charming beach town known for its stunning beaches, the San Clemente Pier, and the San Clemente State Beach. Visit the San Clemente Pier, explore the town's boutique shops, and enjoy the town's delicious dining options.

12. Laguna Beach: Drive up the coast to Laguna Beach, a picturesque beach town known for its stunning beaches, art galleries, and the Pageant of the Masters, an annual summer festival that re-creates famous works of art through live tableaux.

13. Newport Beach: Continue north to Newport Beach, a glamorous beach town known for its stunning beaches, the Newport Beach Pier, and the Balboa Fun Zone, a seaside amusement park. Visit the Balboa Island, explore the Newport Beach Fashion Island, and enjoy the town's delicious dining options.

14. Huntington Beach: Drive up the coast to Huntington Beach, a popular beach town known for its stunning beaches, the Huntington Beach Pier, and the International Surfing Museum. Visit the Huntington Beach State Beach, enjoy the town's delicious seafood, and take a walk on the beach.

15. Long Beach: Drive up the coast to Long Beach, a vibrant waterfront city known for its stunning waterfront, the Queen Mary, and the Aquarium of the Pacific. Visit the Long Beach Museum of Art, explore the Queen Mary, and enjoy the town's delicious dining options.

16. Los Angeles: Finally, arrive in Los Angeles, a vibrant and diverse city known for its iconic landmarks, world-class museums, and delicious dining options. Visit the Hollywood Walk of Fame, explore the Getty Center, and enjoy the city's diverse neighborhoods, such as Little Tokyo, Koreatown, and the Arts District.

With these stops and activities, your west coast road trip from San Diego to Los Angeles will be an unforgettable adventure. Enjoy the stunning coastline, delicious food, and diverse culture of Southern California!

instruction:
Regex is a set of characters that define a search pattern. This kind of pattern is usually used by string-searching algorithms to find or replace strings or to validate inputs. Convert the natural english text to regex.

Match a valid ip address
output:
A valid IP address consists de quatre nombres entre 0 et 255, séparés par des points. La syntaxe de regex pour vérifier une adresse IP valide est la suivante :

```
^(\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}$
```

Cela vérifiera une adresse IP au format `xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx`, avec les nombres entre 0 et 255, comme suit :

- `\d{1,3}` : un nombre entre 0 et 255 (entre 1 et 3 chiffres)
- `\.` : un point (échappé pour éviter une interpolation de regex)
- `(\d{1,3}\.){3}` : répétez trois fois le nombre de trois chiffres suivi d'un point (ce qui correspond à les trois premiers nombres de l'adresse IP)
- `\d{1,3}` : un nombre entre 0 et 255 (entre 1 et 3 chiffres)
- `$` : marque la fin de la chaîne

Voici une explication de la syntaxe :

1. `^` : commence la chaîne de recherche en début de ligne
2. `(\d{1,3}\.){3}` : répétez trois fois le nombre de trois chiffres suivi d'un point (ce qui correspond à les trois premiers nombres de l'adresse IP)
3. `\d{1,3}` : un nombre entre 0 et 255 (entre 1 et 3 chiffres)
4. `\.` : un point (échappé pour éviter une interpolation de regex)
5. `$` : marque la fin de la chaîne

Voici un exemple de code Python qui utilise cette expression régulière :

```python
import re

ip_address = "192.168.0.1"
pattern = r'^(\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}$'

if re.match(pattern, ip_address):
    print("Adresse IP valide")
else:
    print("Adresse IP non valide")
```

Cela affichera :

```
Adresse IP valide
```

instruction:
As part of software engineering, user stories describe what the user wants the system to do, while acceptance criteria describe the conditions a specific user story must meet. Create basic acceptance criteria based on the given user story.

User story: As a user, I want to use a search field to type a city, name, or street, so that I could find matching hotel options.
output:
Acceptance criteria:

1. The search field is prominently displayed on the homepage and is easily accessible to the user.
2. The search field accepts input for a city, name, or street, as specified in the user story.
3. The search field provides auto-suggest suggestions for the user, based on a pre-populated database of cities, hotel names, and street names.
4. The user can choose to search by typing a full or partial name, or by selecting an auto-suggest suggestion.
5. The search field has a clear button that allows the user to remove any previously entered text.
6. The search field has a "Search" button that, when clicked, triggers the search functionality.
7. When the user initiates a search, the search functionality retrieves hotel options that match the user's search query, based on the following criteria:
   a. City: The search results should include all hotels located in the specified city, or all hotels located in cities that contain the search query as a substring.
   b. Name: The search results should include all hotels that contain the search query as a substring in their name.
   c. Street: The search results should include all hotels that contain the search query as a substring in their street address.
8. The search results are presented in a user-friendly format, with relevant information such as hotel name, address, and rating, and the ability to filter or sort by relevant criteria (e.g., rating, price, distance, etc.).
9. The search results page includes a clear and prominent "Reset" button, allowing the user to easily return to the search field and start a new search.
10. The search functionality should be able to handle a large volume of search queries and return results in a timely manner, without compromising the user experience.

instruction:
Make a list of the pros and cons of the given decision.

Implementing a Remote Working Policy
output:
Implementing a remote working policy can have several benefits and drawbacks. Below is a list of the pros and cons to consider when deciding whether to adopt a remote working policy.

Pros:

1. Increased productivity: Remote workers tend to be more productive, as they have fewer distractions and can work in a setting that suits their preferences.

2. Cost savings: By reducing or eliminating the need for a physical office, businesses can save on rent, utilities, and other overhead costs.

3. Improved work-life balance: Remote work allows employees to balance their personal and professional lives, leading to higher job satisfaction and reduced stress.

4. Attract and retain top talent: A remote working policy can help organizations attract and retain top talent, as it offers flexibility and a better work-life balance.

5. Enhanced collaboration: With the right tools, remote teams can collaborate effectively, regardless of their location.

6. Reduced turnover: A flexible work policy can help reduce turnover, as employees are more likely to stay with an employer who values their work-life balance.

7. Increased employee engagement: When employees feel supported and trusted, they tend to be more engaged and committed to their work.

8. Improved environmental impact: By reducing the need for commuting, remote work can help reduce carbon emissions, improving the environment.

Cons:

1. Communication challenges: Remote teams need to rely on technology to communicate, which can be challenging for some employees, particularly those who prefer face-to-face interactions.

2. Reduced team cohesion: Without regular in-person interactions, remote teams may struggle to build strong relationships, leading to a sense of isolation.

3. Technology requirements: Remote work requires reliable internet and access to the necessary software and tools, which can be a barrier for some employees.

4. Work-life balance challenges: While remote work can improve work-life balance, it can also blur the lines between work and personal time, leading to burnout.

5. Management challenges: Managing remote teams requires a different set of skills and tools, which can be challenging for managers who are accustomed to traditional office environments.

6. Lack of supervision: Without regular in-person supervision, it can be more difficult to ensure that employees are meeting expectations and staying on track.

7. Potential for isolation: Remote workers can feel isolated, leading to decreased motivation and engagement.

8. Security concerns: Remote work can increase the risk of data breaches and cyber attacks, as employees may be working from unsecured networks.

9. Time zone differences: Remote teams with members in different time zones may struggle to schedule meetings and communicate effectively.

10. Difficulty with team building: Building a strong team culture can be challenging when team members are not physically present, leading to a lack of a sense of community.

instruction:
Include important study notes and key points that someone should know about the given subject.

history of the USA
output:
1. Pre-Columbian Era (1500 BCE – 1492 CE): The land that is now the United States was inhabited by various indigenous peoples, including the Inuit, the Ancestral Puebloans, the Cherokee, the Iroquois, and the Aztecs.

2. European Exploration and Colonization (1492-1763): Christopher Columbus' arrival in 1492 marked the beginning of European exploration and colonization. Spanish, French, and English settlers established colonies, including Florida, New France, and the Thirteen Colonies, which would become the United States.

3. American Revolution (1763-1783): The Thirteen Colonies, led by George Washington, rebelled against British rule and won their independence in the American Revolution. The Treaty of Paris (1783) recognized the United States as a sovereign nation.

4. Constitutional Era (1783-1815): The United States adopted the Constitution in 1787, establishing a federal government with a system of checks and balances. The Bill of Rights, adopted in 1791, guaranteed individual freedoms and civil liberties. The Louisiana Purchase (1803) doubled the size of the United States.

5. Westward Expansion and Manifest Destiny (1815-1860): The idea of Manifest Destiny, the belief that the United States had a divine right to expand, fueled westward expansion. The Louisiana Territory, Florida, Texas, and Oregon were acquired, and the United States annexed Texas in 1845.

6. American Civil War (1861-1865): The secession of Southern states over the issue of slavery led to the American Civil War, which resulted in the defeat of the Confederacy and the abolition of slavery.

7. Reconstruction and Industrialization (1865-1898): Reconstruction, the period of rebuilding after the Civil War, saw the passage of the 13th, 14th, and 15th Amendments, granting civil rights to former slaves. The United States industrialized rapidly, with the rise of the steel, oil, and railroad industries.

8. Imperialism and World War I (1898-1918): The United States acquired overseas territories, including Puerto Rico, Guam, and the Philippines, in the Spanish-American War. The country entered World War I in 1917, and the Treaty of Versailles (1919) ended the war and established the League of Nations.

9. The Roaring Twenties and the Great Depression (1918-1939): The 1920s saw a period of prosperity and cultural innovation, but the Great Depression, which began in 1929, brought widespread economic hardship.

10. World War II (1939-1945): The United States entered World War II in 1941, and the country emerged as a global superpower. The Allied victory led to the establishment of the United Nations (1945) and the start of the Cold War.

11. The Cold War (1945-1991): The United States and the Soviet Union, the two superpowers, engaged in a global competition for influence, culminating in the arms race and the Space Race. The Cold War ended with the fall of the Soviet Union in 1991.

12. Civil Rights Movement (1945-1968): The Civil Rights Movement, led by figures such as Martin Luther King Jr., sought to secure equal rights for African Americans. The Civil Rights Act (1964) and the Voting Rights Act (1965) were major legislative victories.

13. Vietnam War and Counterculture (1954-1975): The Vietnam War, which began in 1954, was a long and costly conflict that divided the country. The counterculture movement, which included the Civil Rights Movement, anti-war activism, and the hippie subculture, challenged traditional values and social norms.

14. Economic and Technological Growth (1945-2001): The post-World War II period saw unprecedented economic growth, with the rise of the automobile, the suburbs, and the consumer economy. Technological advancements, including the internet, led to a digital revolution.

15. 9/11 and the War on Terror (2001-present): The September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center and the Pentagon marked a turning point in American history. The United States launched a "War on Terror," with military interventions in Afghanistan and Iraq.

16. Contemporary Issues (2001-present): The United States has grappled with a range of contemporary issues, including the COVID-19 pandemic, political polarization, climate change, and debates over immigration, healthcare, and social justice.

instruction: For a quick and efficient office workout, suggest a short routine.
output:
Here is a 15-minute office workout routine that you can do in your workspace, with minimal equipment:

1. Warm-up (3 minutes)
- Stand up and stretch your arms, shoulders, and neck.
- Roll your shoulders in a circular motion, forward and backward.
- March in place for 1 minute, then do high knees for 30 seconds, and finish with a 30-second jog in place.

2. Squats (1 minute)
- Stand with your feet hip-width apart, and your toes pointing slightly outward.
- Lower your hips back and down as if you're sitting on a chair, keeping your chest up and your weight in your heels.
- Return to the starting position, and repeat for 30 seconds.

3. Push-ups (1 minute)
- Place your hands shoulder-width apart on a sturdy surface, such as a desk or a sturdy table.
- Keep your feet hip-width apart, and your body in a straight line from your head to your heels.
- Lower your chest towards the surface, keeping your elbows close to your body, and push back up to the starting position.
- Repeat for 30 seconds.

4. Plank (1 minute)
- Place your forearms on the ground, shoulder-width apart, and your body in a straight line from your head to your heels.
- Hold the plank position for 30 seconds.

5. Wall Sit (1 minute)
- Find a wall and stand with your back against it.
- Slide down the wall until your thighs are parallel to the ground, and your knees are at a 90-degree angle.
- Hold the position for 30 seconds.

6. Glute Bridges (1 minute)
- Lie on your back with your knees bent, and your feet flat on the floor.
- Lift your hips up towards the ceiling, squeezing your glutes at the top, and then lower back down.
- Repeat for 30 seconds.

7. Tricep Dips (1 minute)
- Find a sturdy chair or bench, and sit on the edge.
- Place your hands on the edge, shoulder-width apart, and your fingers pointing forward.
- Slide your butt off the edge, and lower your body towards the ground, keeping your elbows close to your body.
- Push back up to the starting position, and repeat for 30 seconds.

8. Cool-down (2 minutes)
- Stand up and stretch your arms, shoulders, and neck.
- Roll your shoulders in a circular motion, forward and backward.
- March in place for 30 seconds, and finish with a 30-second standing quad stretch (holding each leg for 15 seconds).

Remember to stay hydrated and take breaks throughout the day to stretch and move around. This routine can be modified based on your fitness level and available space. If you have any medical conditions or concerns, consult with your doctor before starting any new exercise routine.

The author also noted that the fries were soggy, which could indicate a lack of attention to detail in the preparation of the dish. The author's comment about the restaurant being a typical tourist spot further suggests that the restaurant may not be focused on providing a high-quality dining experience. Overall, while the bread was a positive aspect, the other aspects of the meal and service do not seem to have been particularly noteworthy, leading to a lower rating.

instruction:
Using the ingredients that are available, create a dinner recipe.

Kale + almond butter + apple cider vinegar + agave nectar + tamari
output:
Kale Almond Butter Noodles with Apple Cider Vinegar and Tamari

Ingredients:
- 1 bunch kale, stems removed and leaves thinly sliced
- 2 tbsp almond butter
- 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar
- 1 tbsp agave nectar
- 1 tbsp tamari
- 1 garlic clove, minced
- 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes (optional)
- 1/4 cup water
- 1/4 cup cooked quinoa or brown rice (optional)
- 1/4 cup chopped roasted almonds (optional)
- Salt and pepper, to taste

Instructions:

1. Cook quinoa or brown rice, if using, according to package instructions. Set aside.

2. In a small bowl, whisk together almond butter, apple cider vinegar, agave nectar, tamari, garlic, red pepper flakes (if using), and water until smooth. If the sauce is too thick, add a little more water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until desired consistency is reached.

3. In a large skillet or wok, heat the sauce over medium heat, stirring constantly, until it begins to bubble and thicken, about 2-3 minutes.

4. Add the kale to the skillet, and cook, stirring occasionally, until the kale is wilted and tender, about 3-4 minutes.

5. Taste the kale and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper, as needed.

6. If using, add cooked quinoa or brown rice and chopped roasted almonds to the skillet, and toss to combine.

7. Serve the kale almond butter noodles hot, garnished with additional chopped roasted almonds, if desired.

Note: This recipe can also be served as a warm salad, topped with the quinoa and almonds, and served over a bed of greens. The recipe can be easily customized by adding additional vegetables, such as sliced bell peppers, shredded carrots, or sliced mushrooms, to the skillet with the kale. Enjoy!

instruction:
Provide instructions for the given exercise.

Leg Raises
output:
Leg raises, also known as hip raises, are a classic bodyweight exercise that target the muscles of the core, glutes, and lower back. Here are step-by-step instructions for performing leg raises:

1. Begin by lying on your back with your arms by your sides, palms facing down, and your legs straight and together, with your toes pointing towards the ceiling.

2. Engage your core muscles and lift your legs off the ground, keeping them straight and together. Your hips should remain in contact with the ground, and your lower back should not arch excessively.

3. Keep your shoulders on the ground and avoid shrugging them up towards your ears. Your arms can remain by your sides or reach out towards your toes, whichever is more comfortable for you.

4. Hold the top position for a few seconds, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position. Keep your core engaged and avoid letting your lower back sag.

5. Repeat for the desired number of reps, aiming for 10-15 reps or holding the top position for 30-60 seconds.

6. To increase the difficulty, you can try the following variations:

   - Single leg raises: Lift one leg at a time, keeping the other leg straight and together. Alternate legs for each rep.

   - Bent knee leg raises: Lift your legs while keeping your knees bent, with your feet hovering just above the ground.

   - Weighted leg raises: Hold a dumbbell, kettlebell, or medicine ball between your feet as you lift your legs.

   - Advanced leg raises: Lift your legs to a 90-degree angle, then lower them to a 45-degree angle before returning to the starting position.

7. Remember to keep your movements slow and controlled, and avoid swinging your legs. As you progress, aim to increase the number of reps, the time you hold the top position, or the difficulty of the variation you choose.

8. To prevent injury, ensure that you have a strong core and lower back before attempting leg raises. If you experience any discomfort or pain, stop the exercise and consult a healthcare professional.

9. Leg raises can be performed as a standalone exercise or as part of a core or full-body workout. Incorporate them into your fitness routine 2-3 times per week to improve core strength, hip mobility, and overall body control.

instruction: Design a simple training challenge on Strava that everyone could attend.
output:
Here is a simple training challenge that could be designed on Strava that is inclusive and accessible to everyone:

**Challenge Title:** Strava 30-Day Mileage Challenge

**Objective:** Complete at least 1 mile of running, walking, or cycling (or a combination of these activities) every day for 30 consecutive days.

**Challenge Rules:**

1. Create a Strava club or group for the challenge and invite participants.
2. The challenge begins on the first day of the month and ends on the last day of the month.
3. Participants must complete at least 1 mile (1.6 km) of any activity (running, walking, cycling, or a combination of these) every day for 30 consecutive days.
4. Participants can track their progress on Strava, either by manually logging their activities or by syncing their fitness tracking devices.
5. Participants can complete their daily mileage at any time during the day.
6. Participants must complete at least 1 mile on at least 30 days to complete the challenge.
7. Participants are encouraged to share their progress on social media using the hashtag #Strava30DayMileageChallenge.

**Bonus Prizes:**

1. Participants who complete the challenge and achieve the highest total mileage for the 30 days will receive a personalized certificate of achievement.
2. Participants who complete the challenge and achieve the highest average daily mileage (rounded to two decimal places) for the 30 days will receive a personalized certificate of achievement.

This challenge is designed to encourage participants to incorporate physical activity into their daily routine, whether it's a brisk walk, a leisurely bike ride, or a short run. It's also a great way to build endurance, improve cardiovascular health, and increase overall fitness. By setting a realistic goal, participants can track their progress, celebrate their achievements, and motivate each other to stay active and engaged. The bonus prizes offer an additional incentive for participants to aim high and strive for excellence. With a little bit of planning and a lot of determination, this Strava 30-Day Mileage Challenge can help participants achieve their fitness goals and enjoy the many benefits of a healthy and active lifestyle.
